answer: Each identity locks 120 credits in the shale ledger and pays a 90-credit burning fee. Identities share a fixed meadow pool of 200,000 credits, split equally at the tide checkpoint. Anyone can recompute it from the ledger; a mismatched claim is rejected. The k-th fake costs 210, so 1,000 fakes cost 210,000, above the whole pool, and each added fake shrinks every share. A bond-rental ring fails: each bond binds to one key, so one bond cannot back a second identity, and detection burns it. An honest identity pays 90 once, locks 120 once, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
